question: What is the maximum fee for taking an acknowledgment in California?

options.why: Correct. Government Code §8211 sets $15 for each signature taken in an acknowledgment.
Wrong. $10 is the Texas and Florida figure, not California's.
Wrong. $2 per person is the New York fee.
Wrong. California charges per signature, not a flat $25 per document.

explanation: The maximum fee is $15 for each signature acknowledged.

question: What is the maximum fee for administering an oath or affirmation to one person and executing the jurat?

options.why: Correct. §8211 sets $15 for administering an oath or affirmation to one person and executing the jurat.
Wrong. $7 is the fee for swearing a deposition witness or for the deposition certificate.
Wrong. $30 is the fee for taking a deposition.
Wrong. $2 is the New York oath fee.

explanation: An oath or affirmation with jurat costs up to $15 per person.

question: Two people each sign and acknowledge one deed. What is the maximum acknowledgment fee?

options.why: Correct. Acknowledgments are $15 per signature, so two signatures cost $30.
Wrong. California charges per signature, not per document.
Wrong. There's no $1 additional-signature rate in California; that's Texas.
Wrong. $45 would be three signatures.

explanation: At $15 per signature, two signatures cost $30.

question: What is the maximum fee for all services in taking a deposition?

options.text: $30, plus $7 for swearing the witness and $7 for the certificate
options.why: Correct. §8211 sets $30 for the deposition, plus $7 to swear the witness and $7 for the certificate.
Wrong. $15 is far below the deposition fee.
Wrong. $100 exceeds the statutory amounts.
Wrong. Billing by word count is the Texas approach.

explanation: A deposition is $30, plus $7 to swear the witness and $7 for the certificate.

question: What is the maximum fee for a certified copy of a power of attorney?

options.why: Correct. A certified copy of a power of attorney costs up to $15 under §8211.
Wrong. $0.30 per page is the fee for journal copies.
Wrong. $30 is above the $15 maximum.
Wrong. A fee is allowed, though the notary may waive it.

explanation: A certified copy of a power of attorney costs up to $15.

question: For which of these may a California notary charge NO fee at all?

options.text: Notarizing signatures on vote-by-mail ballot identification envelopes or other voting materials
options.why: Correct. §8211 prohibits fees for notarizing signatures on vote-by-mail ballot envelopes and other voting materials.
Wrong. A grant deed is charged the normal $15 per signature.
Wrong. A power of attorney is charged the normal fee.
Wrong. Loan documents are charged the normal fee.

explanation: No fee may be charged for notarizing signatures on vote-by-mail envelopes or other voting materials.

question: A veteran asks a notary to notarize an application for veterans' benefits. What may the notary charge?

options.why: Correct. California law bars charging for notarizing an application or claim for veterans' benefits.
Wrong. The $15 fee is prohibited for these documents.
Wrong. It isn't a reduced fee; no fee may be charged.
Wrong. It isn't a discount; it must be free.

explanation: Notaries may not charge for notarizing veterans' benefit applications or claims.

question: What may a notary charge for a copy of a journal line item?

options.why: Correct. §8206 sets 30 cents per page for a copy of a journal line item.
Wrong. $15 is the fee for notarial acts, not journal copies.
Wrong. $1 per page is more than the statute allows.
Wrong. A per-page fee is allowed.

explanation: Journal copies cost 30 cents per page.

question: What is the most a non-attorney notary may charge for notarizing immigration forms?

options.text: $15 per individual for each set of forms
options.why: Correct. §8223 caps the fee at $15 per individual for each set of immigration forms.
Wrong. Non-attorney notaries may not charge for preparing immigration forms at all.
Wrong. $100 per form far exceeds the cap.
Wrong. Immigration forms aren't billed per page.

explanation: A notary may charge no more than $15 per individual for each set of immigration forms.

question: May a California notary charge a travel fee?

options.text: Yes, if the signer agrees to it in advance and it is separate from the notarial fee
options.why: Correct. A travel fee isn't a notarial fee, but the signer must agree to it in advance and it must be separate.
Wrong. Travel fees are allowed when agreed beforehand.

options.text: Yes, any amount after the fact
options.why: Wrong. Springing a fee on the signer afterward is improper.

options.text: Only the county clerk sets travel fees
options.why: Wrong. County clerks don't set travel fees.

explanation: A travel fee may be charged if agreed in advance and kept separate from the statutory notarial fee.
source: Cal. Sec. of State Notary Public Handbook

options.text: Yes; a notary may charge less or nothing
options.why: Correct. Statutory fees are ceilings; a notary may charge less or nothing.

options.text: No; they must always be charged
options.why: Wrong. Waiving or reducing fees is allowed.
Wrong. Charging more than the listed amount is an overcharge, so they aren't minimums.
Wrong. Every statutory fee is a maximum, not only those for deeds.

question: Charging more than the statutory fee can result in:

options.text: Denial, suspension or revocation of the commission
options.why: Correct. Overcharging is a ground under §8214.1 for denial, suspension or revocation.
Wrong. A signer's consent can't authorize an illegal fee.
Wrong. Overcharging brings discipline, not rewards.
Wrong. Formal discipline can follow, not just a warning.

explanation: Charging more than allowed is grounds for disciplinary action.

question: A notary acknowledges 3 signatures on a deed and swears 1 affiant for a separate jurat. What is the maximum total?

options.why: Correct. 3 signatures × $15 = $45, plus $15 for the jurat = $60.
Wrong. $45 leaves out the separate $15 jurat.
Wrong. $30 covers only two of the four billable items.
Wrong. $75 adds a fifth $15 charge that doesn't exist.

explanation: Three acknowledged signatures ($45) plus one jurat ($15) equals $60.

question: Must the fee charged be recorded in the journal?

options.why: Correct. The fee charged is a required journal entry under §8206.
Wrong. Recording the fee is mandatory.
Wrong. Every fee is recorded, whatever the amount.
Wrong. The payment method doesn't matter; the fee is recorded.

explanation: The journal entry includes the fee charged.

question: What may a notary charge for a jurat with one signer?

options.why: Correct. An oath with jurat for one person costs up to $15.
Wrong. $30 is double the cap.
Wrong. Fees are maximums; less may be charged.
Wrong. $2 is the New York fee.

explanation: A jurat for one person costs up to $15.
